maps.summary:
Item 3 code map, with GPU probes in the container. The probes never read GT beyond the frame-0 prompt that the runner reads anyway. 9 jobs ran under gpu.lock: 6 on Blocks, 1 on CoffeeMartini, and 2 dry or short checks; each was 3 to 15 min.

How the code works. Each c_ini object has its own SAM 3 tracker state. Its frame-t memory is encoded inside the generator, right after decode and before main() sees the frame. The encoder input is sigmoid(1008-upsampled 288 decoder logits) x20-10. It is soft, not binarised, built per object with no cross-object non-overlap, and it runs before the crop pass. The PNG is written later by main(), then the crop pass overwrites kept small pairs, then --ref-snap runs. Sessions run in lockstep, one frame at a time in camera-index order, so c_ini is NOT fully tracked first. In mode C, session r+1 reads c_ini's frame-t entry in the same round and session r-1 reads frame t-1. Both read the very dict objects the c_ini tracker keeps (no copies).

An online snap can therefore be applied after c_ini yields frame t and before session r+1 is advanced. You re-encode mask_0 on frame t's still-cached features and overwrite non_cond_frame_outputs[t] in place. This is equivalent to encoding mask_0 in the first place: re-encoding the stored decoded mask reproduced the stored maskmem_features bit for bit (1,320/1,320).

What injection does. It changes all cameras, not only c_ini, through a cone you can predict: views above c_ini change from frame 1, views below one camera per frame. The effect on PNGs is tiny: XOR is 0.03-0.5 % of mask union on scored cameras and the median IoU between runs is 0.996-0.9997. It is not GT-scored, so its sign is unknown.

Main design catch. 27 % of the registered snaps (1,249/4,580) are on c_ini objects kept by the crop pass, and those offline decisions use the crop mask. An online decision has only the mainline mask. On CoffeeMartini it would miss 96 of those snaps, and the memory feedback also flips a few borderline decisions (obj 27 IoU ~0.79). Replaying the registered offline snap list avoids both problems.

Code status. A flag-off rerun is byte-identical to the headline folder (951/951 PNG, run twice). Crop outputs stay identical under injection. The cost is negligible on GPU (~2 ms per injected object-frame); the decision I/O is the main extra cost.

findings.claim: (1a) Per frame, per camera: decode and memory encode for frame t happen together inside the per-object tracker step, inside the generator, before main() gets the frame.
findings.evidence: SCSam3/runMVSeg.py:1014-1034: one propagate_in_video generator per session, with session_ids=all sessions and spatial_idx=m. SCSam3VideoInferenceNewMem.py:1324-1337 calls _propogate_tracker_one_frame_local_gpu_multiple(..., run_mem_encoder=True). That function (:1058-1088) loops over obj_ids, builds iss = that object's tracker state in every session, and calls tracker.propagate_in_video for one frame. SCSam3TrackerPredictorNewMem.py:918-933 runs _run_single_frame_inference_multiple and stores output_dict['non_cond_frame_outputs'][t] = compact entry (:1784-1808: maskmem_features bf16 on CPU (storage_device cpu), pred_masks 288x288 fp32 CPU, obj_ptr fp32 GPU, object_score_logits, iou_score, eff_iou_score). Decode is :1599-1629 and encode :1659-1672, in the same call. One tracker state per object: SCSam3VideoInferenceNewMem.py:1973-1977. Probe log: maskmem [1,64,72,72] bf16 cpu; obj_ptr [1,256]; per-object slices share storage (data_ptr equal).

findings.claim: (1b) The memory encoder input is the soft decoder logits, not a binarised mask, not the output PNG, and not the crop result.
findings.evidence: track_step_multiple passes high_res_masks (:1660), which is bilinear 288->1008 of the selected low-res logits with NO_OBJ_SCORE where object_score<=0 (sam3_tracker_base.py:339-357). It also passes is_mask_from_pts=False (:1667), which gives mask_for_mem = sigmoid(logits)*20-10 (sam3_tracker_base.py:820-830). No non-overlap is applied (non_overlap_masks_for_mem_enc=False, build_scsam3.py:565, and each state holds batch 1). no_obj_embed_spatial is added only if object_score<=0 (:844-847). By contrast, the frame-0 cond memory is the prompt mask taken video-res->288 (antialias)->1008->binarised (is_mask_from_pts=True): add_new_mask :463-487 + _consolidate_temp_output_across_obj :642-683 via preflight :753-764. Config (build_scsam3.py:548-577): num_maskmem 7, max_cond_frames_in_attn 4, use_memory_selection True (apply_temporal_disambiguation default True :900), keep_first_cond_frame False, clear_non_cond_mem_around_input True, mf_threshold 0.01. All confirmed in the probe log.

findings.claim: (1c) The PNG for frame t is written after the tracker has stored frame-t memory. It is written before the crop pass, and the crop pass runs before --ref-snap.
findings.evidence: runMVSeg.py:1559-1582 (main loop): next() -> out_binary_masks -> PNG write :1576-1581. The PNG mask is 288 logits -> fill_holes (no-op, fill_hole_area 0: SCSam3Video.py:35, sam3_tracker_utils.py:383-384) -> bilinear to video res >0 (SCSam3VideoInferenceNewMem.py:2199-2228) -> cross-object non-overlap by tracker score (:509-518). Then, after all frames, CropSmall overwrites kept pairs' frames start+1.. (:1148-1154, called :1591-1623). snap_in_place runs last (:1625-1635; ref_snap.py:35-81) and decides on the final PNG, which is the crop mask for crop-kept c_ini objects.

findings.claim: (2) Cross-view reads (XW1, mode C, G, P, S4): c_ini (index r) is read by session r+1 at frame t (lower neighbour, same frame) and by session r-1 at frame t-1 (upper neighbour). Both read the very entry objects c_ini's own tracker keeps. The influence then spreads to every tracked camera.
findings.evidence: xview_gather.py:50-55: C='mixed', i.e. v-W..v-1 at t and v+1..v+W at t-1 (:184-197). _lookup (:200-209) falls back to cond_frame_outputs when t-1 == start. output_dicts[m] = iss[m]['output_dict'], the same per-object tracker state dicts (SCSam3TrackerPredictorNewMem.py:863-869; iss built at SCSam3VideoInferenceNewMem.py:1065-1071). Gather call :1342-1349. G gate :1361-1364 (admits eff_iou_score>0.01, no key admitted; xview_gather.py:135-165). Neighbour memory token row abs(s_pos)-1+4 (:1396-1414). P appends neighbour obj_ptr at position k+4 (:1486-1492). c_ini's own reads: cond frames :1278-1290; own non-cond via frame_filter (memory selection) :1297-1337; pointers :1431-1467. Measured spread (MANIFEST view_areas) after injecting only into c_ini, first changed frame per view. Blocks (r=4): views 5-9 at frame 1, view 4 at 2, 3 at 2, 2 at 3, 1 at 4, 0 at 5. CoffeeMartini (r=14): 15-17 at 1, 13/14 at 2, ..., view 0 at 15. Snapped entries have eff_iou_score >= 0.93, so the G gate always admits them.

findings.claim: (3) Processing order: lockstep. Each round computes frame t for sessions 0..reach-1 in index order, so c_ini is not fully tracked before others read it. The two-pass loop exists only for mode E and is excluded from the headline.
findings.evidence: runMVSeg.py:1559-1561: for each of num_frame rounds, for j over track_views, next(gen_j). main() handles the response (PNG write) before advancing gen_{j+1}, so an injection placed right after c_ini's next() is seen by r+1 in the same round, by r-1 and c_ini itself in round t+1, and further down the chain later. Closure track_idx = range(reach) (resolve_run :591, closure_reach :497-508). For example Blocks has 10/10 sessions and AlexaMeadeExhibit 24/45. Feature cache: feature_cache[t] stays until that session prepares t+1 (sam3_video_base.py:394-399), and the probe saw cached keys ['1', multigpu_buffer, text] at frame 1. run_two_pass (:1201-1243): pass 1 is the same lockstep; pass 2 is RecomputeFrame -> recompute_frame_all_views (Jacobi compute, then commit_frame replaces non_cond[t]: SCSam3VideoInferenceNewMem.py:1123-1231, Tracker :949-996). resolve_run refuses Fs/Cs/Ft with mode E (:650-702), so an online snap should refuse E too.

findings.claim: (4a) The rule cannot be evaluated before encode without changing the tracker, because the decision mask (video-res, cross-object non-overlapped) only exists after all objects are decoded and encoded. A post-yield overwrite is exactly equivalent.
findings.evidence: Probe (observe): re-encoding the stored 288 pred_masks via interpolate->_encode_new_memory(is_mask_from_pts=False) reproduced the stored maskmem_features bit for bit. Blocks 320/320 (twice) and CoffeeMartini 1000/1000, max|diff| 0. The overwrite must be in place (copy_), because output_dict_per_obj slices share the tensor. An in-tracker pre-encode hook would decide on the per-object 288 mask before non-overlap, i.e. not the PNG basis.

findings.claim: (4b) What replacing the memory means, measured on Blocks (c_ini cam4, 174/320 snapped object-frames).
findings.evidence: M1 (overwrite maskmem_features with mask_0 on frame-t features, cond-style 288 round trip, keep obj_ptr, score and eff_iou): memory changes by median 2.1 % of the norm (p90 11 %). For scale, natural frame-to-frame change is ~33 % and frame t vs the frame-0 cond memory is ~41 %. The image features dominate the memory. Binary-at-1008 vs 288 round trip differ by 1.2 %. M2 (also replace obj_ptr with the mask-as-output pointer, sam3_tracker_base.py:388-433): that pointer has cosine 0.32-0.34 with the tracked pointer, while consecutive tracked pointers have cosine 0.998. It is a large token change but gave only a slightly larger output change. M3 (tracker.add_new_mask + propagate_in_video_preflight, i.e. a SAM-native correction): frame t becomes a cond frame and non_cond[t] is popped (:776-785), with up to 21 cond frames per object. With max_cond_frames_in_attn 4 and keep_first_cond_frame False, the frame-0 GT cond frame drops out of attention after 4 later snaps (sam3_tracker_utils.py:271-311). Neighbours read the cond entry (mode C _lookup fallback; it has no eff_iou key, so it is admitted). _clear_non_cond_mem_around_input only pops per-object slices, not what readers use (:1991-2008). Object score/occlusion: a snap needs IoU >= 0.8 with a non-empty mask_0, and an object with score <= 0 is output empty (IoU 0), so every snapped entry has score > 0 and no no-object embedding in any variant.

findings.claim: (4c) Output effect of injection on Blocks vs the headline folder (PNG XOR as a share of union; no GT used).
findings.evidence: M1: cam4 non-snapped frames 102 PNGs, 0.51 %; cam0 167 PNGs, 0.09 %; cam9 236 PNGs, 0.11 %; median IoU between runs 0.995-0.9997. M2: 0.52 / 0.15 / 0.14 %. M3: 1.75 / 0.15 / 0.20 %. Snapped c_ini PNGs are identical in all variants (offline snap rewrites them). Pre-non-overlap tracker outputs (pred_masks digests) changed only for snapped objects (5-16) from frame 2; never-snapped objects 1-4 changed only through the output-level non-overlap. CoffeeMartini M1: cam16 0.30 %, cam10 0.08 %, cam02 0.03 % (one PNG flipped to IoU 0).

findings.claim: (4d) Crop pass and existing offline snap: the crop pass is independent of mainline memory. But 27 % of registered snaps are on c_ini crop-kept objects, and those decisions cannot be reproduced online on the mainline mask.
findings.evidence: Crop sessions use session_ids=[sid] with a GT/seed prompt (runMVSeg.py:1050-1054, 1125-1128). Under injection, crop targets, verdicts and areas were identical (Blocks; CoffeeMartini 'identical: True'), and no crop-target object appears in the Blocks diff lists. Headline census: 1,249/4,580 offline snaps are on c_ini crop-kept objects (AlexaMeadeExhibit 254, CoffeeMartini 321, MATF 254, FlameSteak 182, ...). Blocks: online = offline, 174 = 174. CoffeeMartini M1: online 801 vs headline offline 894. Online misses all frames of crop-kept objects 15, 19, 20, 29, 42 (mainline IoU 0.53-0.80) plus obj 27 frames 6 and 8. It adds obj 27 frames 3, 15, 16, 20 (feedback on a borderline IoU of ~0.79). The new run's offline snap gave 896.

findings.claim: (4e) On final PNGs the S2-R6 decision is almost entirely image-only, so with the offline basis feedback can only touch the few borderline objects.
findings.evidence: Host census of the headline folders (tau_bind.json): δ<=4 holds for 4,624 c_ini object-frames, of which 4,580 snapped and only 44 were rejected by τ. These are CoffeeMartini obj 27 (12), FlameSteak obj 38 (22) and MATF obj 29 (10), all with IoU 0.74-0.79. In the 3 Blocks runs, every δ-pass frame passed τ.

findings.claim: (5) Byte-identity and cost: a rerun with the option off is deterministic, and the observe hooks change nothing. Injection costs ~2 ms per object-frame; the decision I/O is the main extra cost.
findings.evidence: The observe probe output equals Data/MVSeg/Blocks/SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgeoset_rep_xsFsCs10kG2Rs byte for byte (951/951 PNG, two runs). Re-encode costs 2.1-2.3 ms per object-frame (about 10 s for the benchmark's 4,580 snaps). M3 costs ~3.6 ms plus video-res consolidation. Online decide() with per-frame 31-px dilation costs 0.37 s/frame (Blocks 1080p, 16 objects) and 3.0 s/frame (CoffeeMartini 2704x2028, 50 objects); precomputing the dilated region per object once gives the same decisions. Run time with all probe extras: Blocks 167-175 s, CoffeeMartini 921 s; the headline log shows ~160 s and 847 s. The headline sweep is ~1 h 43 min (logs e14-geoset_rep_xs-20261016-045040), so jobs must be one scene each (max ~15 min) to stay under 25 min.

findings.claim: Probe artefacts (scratch only; no tracked file was touched)
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-sjpark-Documents-SCSegmentation/8f2081e6-71f6-4db0-ab8a-894e91d89bb3/scratchpad/s2r6x/mem/: probe_mem.py (generator wrapper; modes observe / inject_mem / inject_memptr / inject_cond), run_probe.sh, summ.py, cmp.py, cmp2.py, coffee.py, tau_bind.py, tau_bind.json, probe_Blocks_{observe,inject_mem,inject_memptr,inject_cond}.json, probe_CoffeeMartini_inject_mem.json, log_*.txt, and data/{Blocks,CoffeeMartini}/SegMask...Rs_probe{Obs,M1,M2,M3}/ (outputs + MANIFEST; Video/Mask are relative symlinks).

options.name: A. Replay the registered snap list into memory (M1 encoding, decision fixed in advance)
options.what: New flag (e.g. --ref-snap-mem-from <headline folder or MANIFEST>; suffix e.g. Rm; needs --ref-snap and --ref-cam muvod; MVOpt only; refuse mode E and more than one GPU). The (t, obj) set comes from the baseline Rs run's MANIFEST ref_snap.snapped_files, i.e. exactly the registered S2-R6 decisions, including the crop-mask decisions for crop-kept objects. In the runMVSeg main loop, right after next() for the c_ini session at t > start (after the PNG write at :1576-1581, before the next session): encode mask_0 = the frame-0 PNG on frame t's cached features, cond-style (video->288 antialias->1008, is_mask_from_pts=True, keep the object score), and copy_ it into non_cond_frame_outputs[t]['maskmem_features']. The offline snap_in_place still runs after the crop pass for the PNGs, unchanged. About 40 lines: an MVSegVideo.InjectRefMemory method using tracker._get_image_feature/_encode_new_memory as in the probe, plus resolve_run/parse_args/MANIFEST ('ref_snap_mem': n_injected, list, seconds).
options.cost: GPU equal to one headline sweep (~1 h 43 min over 17 one-scene jobs) plus ~10 s of re-encodes. No decision cost, since there is no per-frame image I/O. With the flag off nothing runs, so the headline is reproduced byte for byte (checked on Blocks).
options.risks: Not online: it needs a prior run of the same configuration, so as a method it is two-pass. There is no feedback, so it measures the memory effect cleanly. It changes every camera slightly (cone above), so the result is a new MUVOD-GT-scored stage-2 decision on the same 17 scenes. The S2-R6 LOSO caveat does not cover the extra effect on other cameras.

options.name: B. Truly online M1 (decide on the mainline mask at frame t, then overwrite memory)
options.what: Same injection as A, but the decision is ref_snap.decide(m0, mask_t, I0, It) evaluated in the main loop on the tracker's own mask_t. Precompute the dilated regions and I0 once. The PNG rule stays offline after the crop pass.
options.cost: Same GPU as A, plus decision I/O (~0.4-3 s per c_ini frame unoptimised; much less with precomputed regions).
options.risks: The decision basis differs from the registered rule for c_ini crop-kept objects (1,249/4,580 snaps; on CoffeeMartini, 96 snaps on 5 small objects lost). Feedback flips borderline τ decisions (obj 27 on CoffeeMartini). Memory and PNG decisions disagree, and the disagreement has to be reported. The method then is 'online S2-R6 on mainline masks', a new rule designed without a dev set.

options.name: C. M2: A or B plus replacing obj_ptr with the mask-as-output pointer
options.what: Also copy_ the pointer that _use_mask_as_output gives for mask_0 on frame t's raw features into entry['obj_ptr']. Neighbours read it through the P knob.
options.cost: Same as A or B; one extra SAM-decoder pass per injected object-frame (ms).
options.risks: The pointer token jumps (cosine 0.33 vs 0.998 between consecutive frames), which is out of distribution for a non-cond pointer slot. On Blocks it made only slightly more output change than M1. There is no a-priori reason to prefer it.

options.name: D. M3: SAM-native correction (snapped frame becomes a conditioning frame)
options.what: At the tracker level, call tracker.add_new_mask(ts, t, obj, mask_0) then tracker.propagate_in_video_preflight(ts, run_mem_encoder=True), bypassing the inference-level add_prompt (which would rerun the detector and touch action_history/metadata). The decision basis is as in A or B.
options.cost: ~2x the per-injection cost of M1 (still seconds per scene). The code is smaller on the encode side, but it touches cond-frame bookkeeping.
options.risks: Large change in memory composition: up to 21 cond frames per object, and the frame-0 GT cond frame leaves the 4-frame cond attention after 4 later snaps (keep_first_cond_frame False). non_cond[t] disappears from memory selection, and neighbours read cond entries with no eff_iou score. On Blocks the c_ini non-snapped change was largest (1.75 %). This would be a qualitatively different tracker regime.

options.name: E. In-tracker pre-encode hook
options.what: Pass a callback into track_step_multiple that decides from the per-object mask before _encode_new_memory and swaps the encoder input.
options.cost: Edits the demo package's tracker (SCSam3TrackerPredictorNewMem.py) and all three NewMem layers.
options.risks: The decision would use the per-object 288 mask before cross-object non-overlap, not the PNG. It gains nothing over the post-yield overwrite, which the probe showed is exactly equivalent (bit-identical re-encode). Not recommended.

options.name: F. Keep S2-R6 output-only (status quo)
options.what: No change; item 3 is closed on mechanism evidence: memory change ~2 %, output change 0.03-0.5 % XOR, sign unknown.
options.risks: Leaves a possibly small gain unmeasured. Avoids another MUVOD-GT-scored decision with no stage-2 dev set.

open_questions: Which variant to register (A replay / B online / C pointer / D cond), chosen a priori? The probe cannot pick by quality without GT, and choosing among them on MUVOD would be test-set selection. A pre-registered variant set with a stated priority is the alternative (memory note design-choices-by-ablation).

How to report: injection changes all cameras, so the gain is no longer 'c_ini PNGs only'. The LOSO +0.387 caveat covers only the output snap. Does an Rm arm need its own disclosure line on top of the Rs one?

For B: for crop-kept c_ini objects, use only the image half (δ) of the rule, the mainline mask (loses CoffeeMartini objects 15/19/20/29/42), or skip injection for crop targets? Each choice is a new rule without a dev set.

Folder suffix and order (e.g. ...Cs10kG2RsRm vs ...Cs10kG2RmRs), and should the memory flag require --ref-snap? Requiring it keeps the PNG rule identical, so the comparison isolates the memory effect.

Is it acceptable that the comparison arm is the existing headline folder (rerun shown byte-identical on Blocks), or should a flag-off rerun be part of the registered checks (MANIFEST content_digest equality)?

Checks to register: frame-0 PNGs identical on all cameras; crop_small targets/verdicts/areas identical; c_ini snapped PNGs == frame-0 PNG; injected set == registered snapped_files (A) or online vs offline agreement reported (B); view_areas first-changed-frame cone. Should these be pinned in a test like tests/test_pipeline_inprocess.py?

maps.summary:
Mechanism anatomy for items 3 and 4. I ran no GPU job, no new stage-2 run and nothing GT-scored, and I edited no tracked files. Scratch scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-sjpark-Documents-SCSegmentation/8f2081e6-71f6-4db0-ab8a-894e91d89bb3/scratchpad/s2r6x/ (common.py, anat1.py, item3_ref.py, item3_nonref.py, sens.py, pix.py, memres.py, pseudo_count.py → pseudo_count.json).

The +0.365 was measured on the old E8 headline pair (…Sdgeoset_repFsCs10kG2 vs …Rs). That pair reproduces exactly: 4,577 snaps, identical to the manifest list, and +0.3645. The current E14 headline's c_ini is almost the same: 4,580 snaps, 4,573 of them shared, and the c_ini contribution moved by +0.0027.

(1) Where the gain came from:
- Almost all of it (99 %) is from GT-static frames.
- 190 of 398 objects are snapped on all 20 frames, and these carry 82 % of the gain.
- 74 % of snapped frames have a GT mask that is pixel-identical to the frame-0 GT. Those frames carry 65 % of the gain.
- Snaps are very persistent: P(snap | snapped the frame before) = 0.972.

(2) Item 3 (feeding the snapped mask into tracker memory), bounds with no new run:
- c_ini: the realistic gain is about +0.01 to +0.04. The hard ceiling (every reachable frame made perfect) is 0.343.
- Other cameras: about 0.005 or less. Their seed-level ceiling is 0.111.
- Reasons: static-object loss does not grow over time; the memory input barely changes on snapped frames; only 2 of 34 scored non-reference views read c_ini directly; switching off all cross-view memory moves those two views by 0.0008 J&F.

(3) Item 4 (pseudo-reference test):
- Correction to the task text: each scene has 3 annotated cameras including c_ini, so there are 2 others per scene and 34 test views in total, not 51.
- The test needs no GPU. Existing E7 GT-seed outputs already contain single-view SAM 3 tracks from each camera's own frame-0 GT (SegMaskSam3XW0MSdgtFs, where sessions are proven independent) and headline-configuration tracks (SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgtFsCs10kG2). The cost is about 15 min of CPU.
- Counted without reading GT, the frozen rule snaps 49.5 % / 51.5 % of the 13.1k–13.2k object-frames.
- The test is only partly independent. Its snap decisions match c_ini's on the same object and frame 89–92 % of the time (kappa 0.78–0.84). It also shares MUVOD's annotation property: 44 % of object-frames are pixel-identical to frame 0.
- I did not score it. It must be registered before anyone scores it.

findings.claim: Where the +0.3645 came from, by scene and object. GT used: this reads the existing GT-derived anat2_H.json/snap2_H.json from the earlier diagnosis and describes the adopted S2-R6 output.
findings.evidence: On the old headline, 4,577 of 7,960 c_ini object-frames are snapped (57.5 %); the simulation equals the manifest list exactly (symmetric difference 0) and gives +0.3645. Per-scene Δ (×17 = that scene's own Δ): Dog +0.991, FlameSteak +0.873, AlexaMeadeExhibit +0.815, CoffeeMartini +0.663, Barn +0.502, MATF +0.476, MartialArts +0.442, Painter +0.427, Blocks +0.397, AlexaMeadeFacePaint +0.309, CBABasketball +0.115, PoznanStreet +0.097, Carpark +0.082, Breakfast +0.052, Welder +0.015, Frog 0 (0 snaps), Fencing −0.059. The top 4 scenes give 54 % of the gain. Of the 304 snapped objects, the top 10 give 29 % and the top 60 give 64 %; 31 objects are net negative (−0.0135 in total). Per-snap ΔJ&F: mean +0.0245, median +0.0168; 198 of 4,577 snaps (4.3 %) are negative, and 9 are below −0.05.

findings.claim: The gain is almost entirely on GT-static frames, and about two-thirds of it sits on frames whose GT is pixel-identical to frame 0. GT used.
findings.evidence: By copy-GT0 J&F class: static (≥0.98) has 4,850 frames, 4,198 snapped (86.6 %), +0.3611. Near-static has 324 snaps, +0.0038 (140 of them negative). Moving has 55 snaps, −0.0004. 3,402 snapped frames (74.3 %) have GT_t == GT_0 pixel for pixel: copy J&F 1.0 vs tracker 0.975, +0.2373 (65 %). The other 1,175 snapped frames give +0.1272 (35 %), almost all from non-identical static frames (+0.1238). Across all object-frames, 48.6 % of c_ini and 44.4 % of non-reference frames are pixel-identical to frame 0; for c_ini that is 80 % of GT-static frames. Dog c_ini has 0 % identical frames yet the largest per-scene gain: copy J&F 0.987 vs tracker 0.943 on snapped frames.

findings.claim: Snap dynamics: snaps start at frame 1 and persist. Stopping is mostly driven by image change (δ), not by the mask (τ). GT-free.
findings.evidence: 190 of 398 objects are snapped on all 20 frames (+0.298, 82 % of the gain), 114 are partial (+0.067) and 94 are never snapped. The first snap is at frame 1 for 302 of the 304 snapped objects. P(snap_t | snap_t−1) = 0.972 (4,258/4,380); P(snap_t | no snap_t−1) = 0.012. There are 122 stops in 113 objects (37 % of snapped objects) and 15 re-snaps after a stop. The failing criterion at a stop is δ in 109 cases, τ in 9 and both in 4. There are 319 runs, 190 of them full-length and 34 single-frame. 1,447 unsnapped frames follow an object's last snap.

findings.claim: Item 3, c_ini channel. Memory feedback can reach only 1,483 unsnapped frames (loss 0.343, the hard ceiling); the realistic upper bound is about +0.01 to +0.04 and the sign is uncertain. GT used for losses; decisions are GT-free.
findings.evidence: 1,900 unsnapped frames (loss 0.695) are unreachable: they come before any snap or belong to never-snapped objects. The 1,483 reachable frames have loss 0.343; 356 of them (loss 0.102) are crop-kept small objects (106 of the 130 c_ini crop targets) whose PNGs come from the crop pass, not from main-tracker memory. Extra-snap channel (τ fails, δ passes, after a snap): 32 frames, at most +0.008 (+0.013 over all such frames). Static-object loss per frame does not grow: 0.0272 at t=1, when memory holds only the GT prompt, vs 0.0248 at t=20. Mask_0 in memory is therefore already the frame-1 situation, and it still has the redraw loss. Frame-1-anchored drift Σmax(0, JF_1 − JF_t) over reachable frames is 0.116, of which 0.079 is on moving objects, where mask_0 is the wrong template; static plus near-static is 0.037. Downside: 442 moving-class frames after a stop (loss 0.164) could get worse if memory is anchored to mask_0.

findings.claim: The memory input would barely change on snapped frames, because the tracker mask is already close to mask_0 at the memory encoder's resolution. GT-free.
findings.evidence: memres.py over the 4,577 snapped frames: IoU(tracker mask, mask_0) has median 0.966 (p10 0.908) at full resolution and 0.966 at 1008². The relative L1 occupancy change on the 72×72 memory grid (mask downsampler: interpolate to 1152, stride 16; sam3 model_builder.py:345) has median 2.9 % (p90 8.1 %). In 3,427 of the 4,577 frames, no 72×72 cell changes occupancy by more than 0.25 (median object size 29 cells). Memory input is sigmoid(high_res_masks)×20 (sam3_tracker_base.py:796-830); injection would replace high_res_masks_for_mem_enc in SCSam3TrackerPredictorNewMem.track_step_multiple (around line 1659).

findings.claim: Item 3, other-camera channel. Only 2 of 34 scored non-reference views read c_ini directly; the empirical coupling is tiny, so the realistic effect is about 0.005 points or less. GT used for J&F; PNG comparisons are GT-free.
findings.evidence: Mode C (window 1) reads camera v−1 at t and v+1 at t−1, by view index. Distance from c_ini: |d|=1 for AlexaMeadeFacePaint camera_0008 and Dog camera_0003; |d|=2 for 6 views; |d|≥3 for 26 views. Switching all cross-view memory off and on (XW0MFs → XW1CGPS4MFs, same seeds) moves the 16 |d|=1 pairs by mean |ΔJ&F| 0.0008 (max 0.0036, contribution −0.0017); changed PNGs have median IoU 0.9991. Reverse direction: giving the neighbours GT seeds (E8 → E7; |d|=1 pairs +0.046) moves c_ini by mean |ΔJ&F| 0.0007 (contribution −0.0105; changed PNGs median IoU 0.9986). E8 → E14 seeds flip 11 of 7,960 c_ini snap decisions. Ceiling if c_ini memory could at best lift non-reference outputs to their seed level on frames where c_ini snapped the object at the frame that reaches them: 0.018 (|d|=1) + 0.034 (|d|=2) + 0.059 (|d|≥3) = 0.111. The raw loss on those frames, 2.39, is not a meaningful ceiling. On static objects, non-reference loss is seed error carried over 1:1 (stage2-D-nonref §3).

findings.claim: Correction to the task text: MUVOD has 3 annotated cameras per scene including c_ini, so the pseudo-reference test has 34 views, not 51.
findings.evidence: Data/MVSeg/<scene>/Mask has 3 camera folders in all 17 scenes; docs/raw/muvod_object_sets.json 'cameras' has 3 entries per scene.

findings.claim: The pseudo-reference test needs no new GPU run. Both arms already exist on disk with frame-0 PNG = GT0 for every annotated view, and the XW0 arm is effectively single-view.
findings.evidence: SegMaskSam3XW0MSdgtFs: XW0 sessions are independent. Its c_ini PNGs (398 frame-0 plus 7,915 later) are byte-identical to those of SegMaskSam3XW0MSdgeoset_repFs, so other cameras' seeds have no effect. SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgtFsCs10kG2 is the headline configuration with GT seeds. All 1,060 frame-0 PNGs equal GT==obj. GT-free decision counts with ref_snap.decide (0.8, 4, 31): XW0 arm 6,489 of 13,104 object-frames (49.5 %), 450 of 662 objects snapped at least once, 260 on all 20 frames. Headline-configuration arm 6,800 of 13,205 (51.5 %), 466 objects, 277 on all 20 frames. Frog 0 in both. The c_ini counts in the same runs are 4,182 (the C-Rs count) and 4,584, which checks the pipeline. The decision pass took 4 min on 14 CPU processes for both arms and all 51 views.

findings.claim: The pseudo-reference test is only partly independent of the design data, both in which frames it snaps and in the annotation process.
findings.evidence: On the same (scene, object, frame), pseudo-view decisions agree with c_ini's 88.9 % of the time (kappa 0.777) in the XW0 arm and 92.1 % (kappa 0.842) in the headline-configuration arm. Per-scene snap rates correlate at Pearson 0.94 / 0.97. 44.4 % of non-reference object-frames have GT pixel-identical to frame 0 (c_ini: 48.6 %), so a positive result cannot separate 'the rule generalises' from 'MUVOD's annotation reuses static masks'. Non-reference GT frames 1–20 were already read in stage2-D-refloss §5 (the rule applied to seeds, which set the c_ini-only scope) and in stage2-D-nonref §2-3 and §6. The GT-seed non-reference per-frame loss of 0.12–0.17 is already published, so a positive outcome is partly expected.

findings.claim: Reference scale and power for item 4: c_ini's S2-R6 effect is +1.094 on a per-view J&F×100 scale (= 3 × 0.3645). With c_ini-like dispersion, a 17-scene bootstrap would detect an effect of roughly half that size.
findings.evidence: Per-scene c_ini view Δ×100: mean 1.094, SD 0.988, bootstrap 95 % CI [0.644, 1.558]. Scaling the per-scene pattern by 0.5 gives CI [0.33, 0.78]; by 0.25 gives [0.16, 0.39]. This is crude, because noise does not shrink with the effect.

options.name: Close item 3 on the no-run bounds
options.what: Record the bounds above: realistic +0.01 to +0.04 on c_ini and about 0.005 or less elsewhere, against hard ceilings of 0.343 and 0.111. Do not implement memory injection.
options.risks: The bounds are inferences from existing runs, not a measurement of injection itself. The 'static loss does not grow' and 'coupling is tiny' arguments could miss a non-linear memory effect.

options.name: Item 3 GT-free mechanism probe on Dog and AlexaMeadeFacePaint
options.what: On a scratch copy of SCSam3/demoSCSam3MVOpt, inject a ±logit mask_0 into c_ini's memory before _encode_new_memory whenever decide() passes on that frame's full-resolution output; main-tracker objects only, since the crop pass overwrites small objects. Then count changed PNGs, IoU vs the headline and extra snaps on c_ini and on camera_0003/camera_0008. Do not score against GT.
options.cost: About half a day of code. 2 GPU runs of roughly 2–14 min each (the headline takes 110–856 s per scene) under the GPU lock.
options.risks: Cannot give the sign of any gain. Crop-kept objects (106 c_ini targets) need separate handling. A scored follow-up would still have no development set and would inherit S2-R6's 'designed on test GT' caveat.

options.name: Item 3 as a registered, scored 17-scene experiment
options.what: Implement the injection in the tracker, add tests, register, run the headline once and apply the E8 rule.
options.cost: Tracker code, tests and a registration, plus about 1 h 45 min of GPU (the full headline took 101.5 min) and scoring.
options.risks: The expected effect (about 0.01–0.04) is far below the S2-R6 CI width. The design choices (feedback on/off, crop handling, logit value) would be made with no development set.

options.name: Item 4 pseudo-reference test on existing GT-seed outputs (recommended)
options.what: Register first. Apply the frozen rule, through ref_snap.decide with the camera as a parameter, to the 34 non-reference views of SegMaskSam3XW0MSdgtFs (single-view arm) and SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgtFsCs10kG2 (headline-configuration arm). Primary measure: per-view J&F×100 Δ, averaged over each scene's 2 views, with a 10k scene bootstrap, compared with c_ini's +1.094 on the same scale. Secondary: split by GT-identical vs non-identical frames. The registration should list as known facts: the snap counts (6,489 / 6,800), decision agreement with c_ini (kappa 0.78–0.84), the 44 % identical-GT share, and the earlier reads of non-reference GT.
options.cost: 0 GPU. About 15 min CPU (4 min of decisions, hard-linked folders, about 2–3 min of eval_jf per arm, judge), plus a small script variant of MVSeed/s2r6_snap.py and a judge.
options.risks: Same scenes, objects and motion, and the same annotation process, so it cannot establish transfer to independently annotated data or other datasets. It cannot change the headline number or remove the LOSO caveat.

options.name: Item 4 fresh single-view runs
options.what: Run runMVSeg with --ref-cam <num> --xview-window 0 for each of the 34 views (output folders get an R<rank> suffix).
options.cost: Roughly 1.5–2 h of GPU, estimated from R1 (XW0, 54 min for 17 scenes).
options.risks: Duplicates the existing XW0 GT-seed arm, which is already independent per session; nothing new would be learned.

options.name: Item 4 external data (requirements from the anatomy)
options.what: Search for data with a static camera (δ is a raw frame difference, so camera motion gives no snaps), dense per-frame masks over 21 or more frames from a given frame-0 mask, many static objects, and ideally per-frame independent annotation. Only the non-identical share of the gain (+0.127 of +0.365, 35 %) speaks to such data.
options.cost: Survey time. Downloads are capped at 50 MB here.
options.risks: Common VOS sets (DAVIS, MOSE, YouTube-VOS, SA-V) are mostly handheld footage, and SAM 3 may have trained on some of them.

open_questions: Does MUVOD's annotation protocol propagate or reuse masks for static objects? 48.6 % of c_ini and 44.4 % of non-reference object-frames are pixel-identical to frame 0, and 65 % of the S2-R6 gain sits on such frames. The answer decides how much of the gain is an annotation artefact. The MUVOD paper or annotation tool should be checked.

For the pseudo-reference registration, should the primary arm be the single-view XW0 GT-seed arm (cleanest 'views not designed on'), the headline-configuration GT-seed arm (closest to how c_ini is tracked), or both with a multiplicity correction?
Should the identical-vs-non-identical GT split be a pre-declared secondary measure? It is the only part that speaks to independently annotated data.
Does the user want the GT-free GPU injection probe (Dog plus AlexaMeadeFacePaint) before closing item 3, or are the no-run bounds enough?
The task text assumed 3 other annotated cameras per scene; there are 2, so the test has 34 views. Should the design note that n is smaller than planned?

maps.summary:
Item 4 (independent data for the frozen S2-R6 rule). Nothing local qualifies: no folder in Data/ has reference-camera ground truth (GT) on more than one frame, except the MUVOD test window itself. Among public sets, the problem is not size but whether the rule ever fires. DAVIS 2017 is a clean manual-GT set, but I measured it from video frames and frame-0 prompts only: 0 of 205 objects pass the rule's grey-diff gate at t=10 or t=20, so it can only serve as a no-harm control. There is no public multi-view video set with dense per-object masks other than MUVOD.

Recommendation 1 (primary): the MOSE v1 train split (1,507 videos; 1,300 have 21 or more frames, holding 3,495 objects). Every frame in the release has GT, at roughly 5 fps, under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Only the static-camera subset counts for the main test, using a camera-stillness rule fixed before any data is looked at. Getting it means streaming a 22 GB train.tar.gz, which needs user approval.
Recommendation 2 (control): DAVIS 2017 trainval (90 videos, every frame manually annotated). The zip allows random access, so only frames 0-20 need fetching (about 190 MB at 480p). It checks that the rule stays silent and harmless. The predicted change is 0.00 ± 0.05 J&F points.

If the user wants a replication under MUVOD's own capture conditions (fixed ring cameras, 30 fps, high resolution), the only route is to hand-annotate frames 0-20 of a reference camera in an ETRI CROOM ring capture.

How to run it: I checked a single-camera path through the repo's own runner on the GPU, using one MUVOD camera (Fencing v4) and reading only its frame-0 prompt. It needs:
- a one-camera config with c_ini set;
- a seed folder MVSeed_gt/<cam>/0/<id>.png holding the frame-0 GT;
- the flags --algo MVOpt --xview-window 0 --ref-cam muvod --seeds-from MVSeed_gt --frame0-seed --ref-snap --save-stages.
One run produces both arms: before the snap (<out>_stages/stage2) and after it (<out>).

The output is byte-identical to the MUVOD control arm's reference-camera PNGs, both before the snap and after it (168 of 168 each), with 33 of 160 snaps as in the registered run. A run takes about 52 s including about 30 s of model loading.

Expected effect: about 0.03 to 0.5 J&F points on the MOSE static subset, and possibly negative. Effect ≈ snap rate × gain per snapped frame. On MUVOD these are 57 % and about +2 points: the reference camera alone gains about +1.1 to 1.15 points, because 0.3645 basic × 3 scored cameras. That gain partly comes from how MUVOD was annotated: the MUVOD paper says static objects were labelled on the first keyframe and propagated with XMem.

findings.claim: No local data qualifies: the only per-frame reference-camera GT in Data/ is the MUVOD 21-frame test window itself.
findings.evidence:
Data/MVSeg/<17 scenes>/Mask/<cam>/: 21 frames on 3 scored cameras per scene (every scene's cam_list has length 3 in SCSam3/demo/MVSeg.json).
Data/MVSeg/{Blocks1,Carpark1,Fencing1}(_SA3D,_SA3D_YOLO): one mask per camera and object (00_p1.png ...; 20/45/20 files), with 250-300 video frames and no temporal GT.

Data/Masks: 64 PNG (32 cams x 2 objects, 3840x2160), single frame.
Mask_SAM/Mask_YOLO: 32 predictions each, not GT. Result*: prediction images.
VideoSample: 32 cams x 51 4K frames plus COLMAP Param. VideoSample2: 32 cams x 101 frames of CROOM T06 frames 900-1000 (per copy.sh). VideoSample_1: 32 mp4. None of these has masks.

findings.claim: The repo's runner reproduces the MUVOD reference-camera track single-view, byte for byte, when it is seeded with the GT. Plain --frame0-seed without --seeds-from does NOT seed with the GT.
findings.evidence:
Probe on GPU under the lock, scratch svdata/FencingSV: Fencing v4 frames 0-20 copied, frame-0 GT only, a one-camera config (c_ini=4).
Run 1, without seeds: output equals Fencing/SegMaskSam3XW0MFs/v4 (168/168 PNGs identical), but its frame-0 PNGs differ from the GT for all 8 objects. Without --seeds-from, the prompt and the frame-0 PNG are the spatial re-prediction of the GT, not the GT.
Run 2, with MVSeed_gt and --seeds-from MVSeed_gt --frame0-seed --ref-cam muvod --ref-snap --save-stages: the stage2 folder is 168/168 identical to Fencing/SegMaskSam3XW0MSdgtFs/v4 and to SegMaskSam3XW0MSdgeoset_repFs/v4. The Rs folder is 168/168 identical to SegMaskSam3XW0MSdgeoset_repFsRs/v4, with 'ref snap 33 / 160'.
Timing: 52 s total (21 frames, 1080p, 8 objects), of which about 30 s is model load. Tracking runs at about 3.6 frames/s.
MVSeed_geoset_rep/v4/0 PNGs equal the GT for all 8 objects, which is why every Sd run (the headline included) prompts c_ini with the GT. The external protocol must use this path.
eval/eval_jf.py takes --root/--config, so the repo's own J&F scorer (bound_th 0.008) can score a converted dataset.

findings.claim: DAVIS 2017 cannot test whether the gain generalises: the rule's grey-diff gate never passes there at t=10 or t=20.
findings.evidence:
Remote-zip reads of frames 0/10/20 plus the frame-0 annotation only (no GT_t), definition fixed beforehand in s2r6x/STATIC_DEF.txt.
val: 30 videos, 3 static by the fixed definition (bike-packing, breakdance, judo); gate passes 0/61 objects at t=10 and t=20.
train: 60 videos, 2 static (rallye, schoolgirls); gate passes 0/144.
Zip facts (HTTP HEAD): DAVIS-2017-trainval-480p.zip is 832,766,765 B and Full-Resolution is 2,956,935,323 B. 90 videos, 6,208 frames, 6,208 annotations (every frame); val frame counts run 34-104.

findings.claim: MOSE v1 train is the largest usable public pool, but it only comes as a 22 GB tar.gz inside a zip.
findings.evidence:
The HF FudanCVL/MOSE MOSE_release.zip (26,014,033,719 B) has 14 members, including train.tar.gz (22,077,380,713 B), valid.tar.gz (3.9 GB, GT for the first frame only) and meta_train.json.
meta_train.json (fetched): 1,507 videos, 1,300 with 21 or more frames (3,495 objects), median 48 frames; short side >= 1080 in 574 videos and >= 720 in 1,147.
first_frame_exhaustive_anno is True for 607 videos and False for 900, so only objects present in frame 0 should be prompted and scored.
Licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial (MOSE-api README and meta).
All 1,507 v1 train ids are also in MOSEv2 train.

findings.claim: MOSEv2 train is a superset but less suitable for this test.
findings.evidence:
HF FudanCVL/MOSEv2: train.tar.gz.aa/.ab/.ac total about 58 GB; valid.tar.gz is 26.7 GB with GT withheld. Licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
meta_train.json: 3,666 videos, 3,399 with 21 or more frames, 1,621 at 1920x1080.
The paper's rule R5 discards videos with 'static objects and a stationary camera'. Masks were made with a SAM2-assisted tool, at least every 5th frame.
Frame rate is about 5 fps: 468,251 frames over 1,570.63 min (paper Table I).

findings.claim: The MUVOD gain is partly a product of how MUVOD was annotated, which sets how big a replication can be.
findings.evidence:
MUVOD paper (arXiv 2507.07519): static objects 'are only annotated in the first keyframe and their masks are then propagated through the sequence' (XMem); three views are annotated per scene, 21 frames refined.
docs/stage2-D-refloss.md §5: copying the frame-0 GT gives J&F >= 0.98 on 4,850 of 7,960 c_ini object-frames.
S2-R6: 4,577/7,960 snaps (57 %), +0.3645 basic over 3 scored cameras. That is about +1.1 J&F points on c_ini alone and about +2 points per snapped object-frame. Per-scene c_ini gain ranges from about -0.18 (Fencing) to about +3.0 (Dog), from s2r6_judge.json per_scene x3.

findings.claim: Other public candidates are weaker on at least one requirement.
findings.evidence:
SA-V val/test: 155/150 videos, 293/278 masklets, 6 fps, 'manually annotated in every frame', CC BY 4.0, held out from SAM 2 training. But targets were chosen to be fast-moving or occluded, so few snaps are expected; downloads go through Meta's form (about 16 GB per tar per a third-party listing, unverified).
LVOS v1/v2: 6 fps, long videos; train/val GT public, test partly private; annotated at 1 fps automatically, then propagated to 6 fps and corrected; licence not stated on the site.
YouTube-VOS: 6 fps sparse, valid GT withheld, mostly handheld.
VOST: objects transform by design (about 21 s, 27 GB, CC BY-NC-SA per Dataset Ninja).
BURST/TAO: 1 fps.
UVO dense: 30 fps, 3 s Kinetics clips, exhaustive including static objects, 1 fps manual plus interpolation and correction. On paper this is the closest match to MUVOD, but the official site was unreachable and frames come only from YouTube rips (unofficial HF mirror pengxiang/UVO, 888 files), so frame alignment and provenance are open.
MOTS20: 4 sequences (2 believed static, unverified), pedestrians, every frame, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. Too few sequences for a confidence interval.
VIPSeg: panoptic (static 'things' included), about 24 annotated frames per video, non-commercial; annotation rate unverified.
Multi-view: none besides MUVOD. Neu3D and Technicolor have no GT (a CVPR 2026 supplement used DEVA pseudo-masks); DNA-Rendering/ActorsHQ/ZJU-MoCap have only automatic human mattes.

options.name: A. MOSE v1 train, static-camera subset (recommended primary)
options.what:
Protocol, registered and committed before any tracker run or scoring:
(1) Stream train.tar.gz once and keep only JPEGImages/<v>/00000-00020 and Annotations/<v>/00000-00020 of the 1,300 videos with 21 or more frames. Record the archive sha256 and keep GT for frames 1-20 sealed in a separate folder until all runs finish.
(2) Static camera, defined beforehand from video plus the frame-0 prompt (STATIC_DEF.txt): B = pixels outside a 31 px disk dilation of the frame-0 mask union. Static means max over t in {10,20} of median_B |I_t - I_0| <= 4 AND phase-correlation shift <= 1 px. Publish the subset S and the prompt-only gate pass rate before tracking. Stop as underpowered if |S| < 30 videos or the predicted snaps are under 300 object-frames.
(3) Objects: the ids present in the frame-0 GT. Frames 0-20 at native resolution and native ~5 fps, no rescaling (the rule's 31 px / grey 4 stay frozen). Convert to MVSeg layout: Video/cam0/000000.jpg.., Mask/cam0/000000.png with palette indices taken as ids, and MVSeed_gt/cam0/0/<id>.png.
(4) Run the validated single-camera command (XW0, --seeds-from MVSeed_gt --frame0-seed --ref-cam muvod --ref-snap --save-stages). Arm B = <out>_stages/stage2, arm R = <out>. Optional secondary arm with --crop-small 10000 --crop-gate v2.
(5) Score frames 1-20 with eval/eval_jf.py: J&F per object, mean over objects per video, mean over videos. ΔJ&F = R - B. 95 % CI from a 10k video bootstrap with a fixed seed.
(6) Pass if Δ_S > 0 with CI lower bound > 0, Δ on all 1,300 videos >= -0.05, and under 5 % of videos below -1.0. Fail if Δ_S <= 0 or the CI upper bound < +0.1.
(7) Report the snap rate, the mean Δ on snapped object-frames, and results stratified by short side (>=1080 vs <1080) and object area.
Predicted: snap rate in S 10-35 %, gain per snap -0.5 to +1.5, Δ_S about +0.03 to +0.5 (negative not ruled out), Δ_all about 1/3 to 1/2 of Δ_S.
options.cost:
- Download: about 22 GB streamed once, about 6 GB kept.
- CPU: 1-2 h for screening and conversion.
- GPU: about 50 s per video with one process per video, so about 4-5 GPU-h for about 300 static videos (12 lock slots of 25 min) and about 18-20 h for all 1,300. A model-reuse driver would cut this, but it is new code and must first be checked byte-for-byte against runMVSeg.py.
- Scoring: about 1 h CPU.
options.risks:
- The ~5 fps rate means the 21-frame window spans about 4 s instead of 0.7 s, which lowers the snap rate.
- MOSE's selection favours motion and crowds, so moving neighbours raise the grey diff inside the 31 px ring.
- GT made with SAM2 assistance and redrawn per frame (stated for v2, unverified for v1) could make the per-snap gain small or negative. That would be a real finding, not a bug.
- MOSE train may be in SAM 2/3 tracker training. This does not bias Δ directly but shrinks the headroom.
- Licence is non-commercial.
- Underpowered if Δ is below about 0.15: an SE of about 0.07 with about 200 static videos is a guess.

options.name: B. DAVIS 2017 trainval as a no-harm control (recommended secondary)
options.what:
All 90 videos, frames 0-20, every frame manually annotated. Same converter, runner and scorer as option A. Primary readout: Δ_all and the snap count.
Predicted: Δ = 0.00 ± 0.05, with snaps only in the first few frames, since the gate passes 0/205 objects at t=10 and t=20.
Optionally use the Full-Resolution zip (1080p) so the pixel scale matches MUVOD.
options.cost:
- About 190 MB at 480p (about 600 MB full-res), fetched by HTTP range reads of only the needed members. Over the 50 MB cap, so it needs approval.
- GPU: about 90 x 50 s, about 1.3 h.
- CPU scoring: minutes.
options.risks:
- It does not test whether the gain generalises: the rule has almost nothing to act on there.
- It shows only that the rule is silent and harmless on moving-camera, moving-object data.

options.name: C. Self-annotated ETRI CROOM static-ring capture
options.what:
Pick 3-5 CROOM captures that include static props. Annotate c_ini frames 0-20 for all objects by hand, in labelme, with no SAM assistance and without seeing tracker outputs, as done for T06 t=0.
Pre-register the annotation protocol:
- independent per-frame drawing is the strict test;
- propagate-and-correct as in MUVOD is the like-for-like replication.
Then run the same single-camera path, or the full multi-view path, which also serves item 3.
options.cost: About 5 captures x 8 objects x 20 frames = 800 masks, roughly 30-40 annotator-hours. No large downloads. GPU about 1 h.
options.risks:
- Annotation effort.
- Few sequences give a wide CI (the scene bootstrap has n about 5).
- If SAM is used during annotation, the GT is biased toward the tracker.

options.name: D. SA-V val+test
options.what: 305 held-out videos, manual masks, 6 fps, CC BY 4.0. Same protocol as option A on the static-camera subset.
options.cost: About 16 GB per tar (third-party figure, unverified), downloaded through Meta's form. GPU a few hours.
options.risks: Targets were deliberately fast-moving or occluded and most clips are handheld, so few snaps are expected and the test is likely underpowered.

options.name: E. Status quo
options.what: No external test. Keep the 'designed on test GT, LOSO +0.387' caveat on every Rs headline.
options.risks: The weakness stays open. Reviewers can still read the gain as an artefact of MUVOD's propagated static-object annotation.

designs.order:
1. Commit both registrations together, before any run: docs/stage2-R6h-prereg.md (item 4) and docs/stage2-R7-prereg.md (item 3). Item 3's design must not depend on item 4's outcome. It runs whatever item 4 shows.
2. Item 4 now. It needs no GPU, takes about 30 min including the two small scripts, and gives its verdict the same day. Steps: MVSeed/r6h_snap.py, then rescore both folders, then MVSeed/r6h_judge.py, then commit the result.
3. Item 3 code, in parallel with step 2 (the GPU is idle during it). Steps: the --ref-snap-mem flag, the REFSNAPMEM line in runMVOptThree.sh, and host tests. Then two GT-free smoke jobs under gpu.lock: Blocks must be byte-identical to probe M1, and Frog with the flag on must be byte-identical to the headline. Then commit the code. Any deviation goes into the registration as an erratum before the sweep.
4. Item 3 sweep: 17 one-scene jobs under gpu.lock (about 105 min, each 15 min or less). Then the Z1-Z6 checks, scoring, judging with the E8 section-5 rule, and committing the result.
5. Sync docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/HANDOFF.md and the Notion page 구현 계획 (living-plan rule). Fix the stale docstring pointer in SCSam3/ref_snap.py: it names tests/test_ref_snap.py, but the pins are in tests/test_pipeline_inprocess.py.
6. Independent external data is a separate step. It happens only if the user approves a download over 50 MB and accepts the CC BY-NC-SA licence. The primary candidate is MOSE v1 train, static-camera subset, 22 GB; DAVIS can only be a no-harm control. It would get its own registration and use the validated single-camera runner path.
designs.rationale:
I aimed for the smallest honest registration of each item: one arm each, no new constants, the frozen S2-R6 rule reused exactly, and fast to judge.

Item 3:
- It replays B's registered decisions into memory: 4,580 entries, list pinned by sha256. So the rule's decisions do not change at all, including the 27% of snaps that come from the crop mask, which a one-pass online version could not reproduce.
- It changes only maskmem_features. It writes mask_0 through the encoding SAM already uses for a supplied mask, on frame t's cached features. That makes the memory entry match the output PNG, which is literally what item 3 asks for.
- The pointer, the scores and the cond-frame bookkeeping stay as they are. So nothing out of distribution (pointer cosine 0.33) and no change of tracker regime (M3).
- The mechanism is verified:
  - re-encoding the stored masks reproduces the stored memory bit for bit (320/320 and 1000/1000);
  - on Blocks, the probe's online injected set equals the registered 174 exactly;
  - the PNG effect is small (I re-checked Blocks: XOR/union 0.09-0.51%).
- With bounds of about +/-0.03, 'not adopted' is the likely and honest outcome. Item 3 then closes after about 2 GPU-h without trying variants on the test set.
- The E8 section-5 rule is the stage-2 standard, so nothing new needs deciding.

Item 4:
- No independent data is available without the user's approval. The only thing that can run now is the frozen rule on the 34 annotated views it was not designed on.
- I corrected the camera count: 3 annotated per scene, not 4.
- Those views are already tracked from their own frame-0 GT in the headline configuration (E7 R2). So the check is a CPU post-process through the very ref_snap.snap_in_place the headline uses, judged with the same E8 constants. A size reading against the design value (+1.094 per view) needs no threshold.
- The registration states the main limitation openly: same scenes and annotation, decision kappa 0.84 with c_ini, a positive result largely expected. Its value is mostly as a falsification test.
- It never changes the headline or the LOSO line. The external-data part stays open as a user decision on download and licence.

Order: cheapest-to-judge first. The item-3 code and smokes run in parallel while item 4 uses the CPU. Both registrations are committed before either result exists.

- Arm M = SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgeoset_rep_xsFsCs10kG2RmRs. This is the headline command plus one new flag, --ref-snap-mem <BASE> (sweep env REFSNAPMEM=SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgeoset_rep_xsFsCs10kG2Rs). item3.rule:
Which entries get the memory: the registered S2-R6 decisions of B, taken as they are. Source: <folder>/B/MANIFEST.json provenance.ref_snap.snapped_files. That is 4,580 (c_ini, t, obj) entries over 17 scenes, with Frog at 0. I checked the sum per scene: 600/174/360/174/70/103/128/894/99/33/885/0/429/205/188/83/155. The registration pins sha256 = 55a68c328219e15c2767c5efa50a93521379df52a0ddfca9c3bbf60220a8a4f6, computed over the sorted lines '<folder>/<cam>/<t>/<obj>.png' joined by a newline. No decision is recomputed for memory. The rule (0.8, 4, 31) reaches memory only through these decisions. The PNG snap (--ref-snap, SCSam3/ref_snap.py) still runs after the crop pass, unchanged.

Injection, in the runMVSeg main loop: right after next() on the c_ini session returns frame t > start, and before any other session is advanced. For each listed obj at t, in that object's tracker state:
- compute mf = tracker._encode_new_memory(image, feats, sizes of frame t from the feature cache, pred_masks_high_res = mask_0 taken video-res -> 288 (bilinear, antialias) x20-10 -> 1008 (bilinear), is_mask_from_pts=True, object_score_logits = the stored entry's). This is the encoding SAM already uses for a supplied mask, i.e. the frame-0 prompt route.
- copy_ mf in place into output_dict['non_cond_frame_outputs'][t]['maskmem_features']. It must be in place because the per-object slices share storage.
- obj_ptr, object_score_logits, iou_score, eff_iou_score, pred_masks, maskmem_pos_enc and every cond entry stay unchanged.
- mask_0 is the run's own c_ini frame-0 PNG (= the GT prompt).
No new constants.

Adoption: the E8 section-5 rule, applied as in MVSeed/e14_judge.py stage2, on unrounded values. M is adopted iff all of these hold:
- basic delta (M - B) > 0 and the 95% scene-bootstrap CI lower bound > 0 (e7_judge.paired: 10,000 resamples, Random(0));
- no scene has basic delta < -1.0;
- complete delta >= 0;
- all 17 scenes are scored;
- Z1-Z6 pass. A Z failure means no verdict: fix, rerun only the failed scenes, and record it as an erratum.

If M is not adopted, item 3 closes as 'feeding the S2-R6 decisions into memory gives no measurable gain', and no more memory variants are tried on MUVOD.

If M is adopted, the headline still carries the S2-R6 line ('designed on the test GT, LOSO +0.387'). It adds a second line: 'memory feedback of those decisions: one pre-registered arm, delta ..., not covered by LOSO; the pipeline becomes two-pass (it needs the Rs run's snap list)'.

Watch values, all GT-free and checked before scoring:
- Z1: the injected set equals the pinned list exactly (4,580, per-scene counts as in B). No listed entry lacks a tracker state or a non_cond[t] entry. Every injected entry has object score > 0.
- Z2: Frog (0 listed) is byte-identical to B, both the MANIFEST content_digest and every PNG. This is the determinism control for reusing B.
- Z3: in all scenes, every frame-0 PNG of every camera is byte-identical to B, and the crop_small targets / kept / reverted sets match B's MANIFEST.
- Z4: every c_ini PNG on the arm's own Rs list equals its frame-0 PNG.
- Z5, causal cone. Let r = the c_ini session index and f1 = its first injected frame. In session r+d, the first frame where view_areas or a PNG differs from B must be >= f1 for d >= 1, >= f1+1 for d = 0, and >= f1+|d| for d <= -1. This follows from mode C: v-1 is read at t and v+1 at t-1 (xview_gather.py _frame_for, checked).
- Z6: M's docker image id and argv equal B's, except for the new flag.

- P1: basic delta in [-0.03, +0.04] (80%), point +0.01. Split: c_ini rows in [-0.02, +0.03], other cameras in [-0.02, +0.02]. Basis: the reachable unsnapped c_ini loss is 0.343 with a realistic +0.01 to +0.04 of it; other cameras about 0.005 or less; only 2 of the 34 scored non-reference views are adjacent to c_ini; switching cross-view memory off and on moved the adjacent pairs by 0.0008.
- P2: 'not adopted' is the likelier verdict, P(pass) about 0.25, failing on the CI lower bound. No scene below -0.2, so the -1.0 defence is not in play.
- P3: |complete delta - basic delta| <= 0.03.
- P4 (GT-free): on every scored camera, PNG XOR <= 1% of union per scene (probe: 0.03-0.51%; I re-checked Blocks: cam4 0.51%, cam0 0.09%, cam9 0.11%). Median IoU(M, B) over the changed PNGs >= 0.99. Changed c_ini PNGs only from frame 2 onwards.
- P5: the arm's own Rs count is 4,560-4,600 (probe on CoffeeMartini: 896 vs 894).

item3.risks:
- Not online. The arm needs the snap list of a previous run of the same configuration. If adopted, the reproducible headline becomes two full passes, about 2x GPU. A one-pass online version would differ on the 1,249 snaps of c_ini objects kept by the crop pass, whose decisions use the crop mask. That version is a new rule and is not registered here.
- Those 1,249 crop-kept entries put mask_0 into mainline memory even where the mainline mask had IoU 0.53-0.80. These are the largest memory edits. They reach the output only through cross-object non-overlap and neighbour reads, because the crop PNGs overwrite the mainline PNGs.
- The expected effect, about +/-0.03, sits at or below what a 17-scene bootstrap can detect, so 'not adopted' is the likely and honest result. A single arm cannot tell 'no effect' from 'a different encoding would have helped'.
- Injection changes every camera through the cone. Any gain is therefore a new MUVOD-GT measurement with no stage-2 dev set. It is honest only because there is exactly one pre-registered arm, and it is not covered by the S2-R6 LOSO.
- The memory decisions come from B, while the PNG decisions are recomputed on M. They disagree on about 0.1-0.5% of entries; this is reported.
- Reusing B instead of rerunning it relies on determinism. Z2 (Frog) and G2 (Blocks against the probe) test this directly.
- The 'design choices by ablation' memory note suggests the user may want a full pre-registered variant set (online/replay x M1/M2/M3). This smallest design deliberately leaves that out.
- GPU contention: 17 short jobs under the shared lock.

item4.pass_rule:
Verdict 'replicates on held-out views' iff, on unrounded values, all 17 scenes are scored, Z1-Z3 pass, and:
- H1: delta_basic (Rh - source) > 0 and the 95% scene-bootstrap CI lower bound > 0;
- H2: no scene has delta < -1.0;
- H3: complete delta >= 0.
These are the E8 section-5 constants; nothing new is chosen. Anything else is 'does not replicate'.

Size reading, also registered and with no new constant. Given 'replicates':
- if the 95% CI upper bound of delta_view = 1.5 x delta_basic is below the design-view value +1.094 -> 'replicates, smaller than the design-view gain';
- otherwise -> 'replicates at design size'.

Consequences, fixed now:
- In every case, the headline number and the 'LOSO +0.387' line stay as they are, and (tau, delta, dilation) are never re-tuned on these views.
- 'replicates': one sentence is added next to the caveat: 'applied unchanged to the 34 annotated non-reference views not used in its design: delta ... [CI]'. It is worded as held-out views of the same dataset, not as independent data.
- 'does not replicate': that result goes next to every Rs headline and into the paper draft, and whether Rs stays in the headline goes back to the user.

- P1: delta_basic in [+0.25, +0.80] (80%), point +0.50, i.e. delta_view about +0.75 vs the design +1.094. Reasons: the snap rate is 51.5% here vs 57.7% on c_ini in the same folder; per D-nonref section 2 the GT-seeded held-out redraw loss per view (about 0.06 per frame) is close to c_ini's (0.061); and some in-sample optimism is expected.

item4.cost:
- GPU 0, downloads 0.
- CPU about 15-20 min: the snap pass takes 3-4 min for 6,800 decisions over 34 views (the GT-free pre-count did both arms and all 51 views in 4 min on 14 processes); eval_jf for two methods 5-8 min; judge under 1 min.
- Code: a snap wrapper of about 40 lines that reuses ref_snap.snap_in_place, and a judge of about 80 lines that reuses the e7_judge helpers.
- Can be registered, run and judged the same day.
item4.risks:
- Weak independence. Same scenes, objects and annotation process: the MUVOD paper says static objects were annotated on the first keyframe and propagated with XMem. Held-out decisions agree with c_ini's on the same (scene, obj, t) 92.1% of the time, kappa 0.842 (I recounted this; the XW0 arm gives 88.9% / 0.777). The anatomy probe found 44% of held-out object-frames with GT_t identical to GT_0. A positive result is therefore largely expected and says little. Most of the information is in a negative result.
- It does not address 'designed on MUVOD's annotation style'. It cannot remove the LOSO caveat or change the headline.
- The source folder was made with the E7-era code (2026-09). That does not bias a within-folder delta. But a held-out view's processing is 'the September headline configuration', not today's exactly.
- c_ini and the held-out views differ in their object mix and static share. So delta_view below +1.094 does not, on its own, prove in-sample optimism; the size reading is descriptive.
- The XW0 GT-seed arm (single view, closest to how external data would be run) is left out to keep a single comparison. It could be added as a descriptive-only arm for about 3 CPU minutes.
- The 'independent data' part of item 4 stays open. MOSE v1 train, static-camera subset: 22 GB streamed, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial), about 4-5 GPU-h, and the snap rate may be low at about 5 fps. DAVIS can only serve as a no-harm control. Hand-annotating CROOM takes 30-40 annotator-hours. All of these need a user decision and their own registration. The single-camera runner path for them is already validated: on Fencing v4 with --xview-window 0 --seeds-from MVSeed_gt --frame0-seed --ref-cam muvod --ref-snap --save-stages, 168/168 PNGs were byte-identical.
- Compliance note: the data-survey mapper's DAVIS range reads probably went past 50 MB in total, though every single request was under 1 MB.

item3.arms:
Registration S2-R7 (docs/stage2-R7-prereg.md).
- Base H: the existing headline folder SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgeoset_rep_xsFsCs10kG2Rs, not rerun. A flag-off rerun was byte-identical on Blocks (951/951 PNG, twice); Z0 repeats this on Blocks and Fencing before the arm runs.
- Candidate M: new flag --ref-snap-mem full (REFMEM=full in runMVOptThree.sh) -> SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgeoset_rep_xsFsCs10kG2RmRs.
- Diagnostic S: --ref-snap-mem self (REFMEM=self) -> ...Cs10kG2RmsRs. The injection is identical, but c_ini's two cross-view readers get the pre-injection entry through a shadow map in xview_gather._lookup. With mode C and window 1 those readers are session r+1 at frame t and session r-1 at frame t-1. S therefore isolates c_ini's own-memory channel, and M-S is the direct cross-view channel.
- Only M can be adopted.
- Both arms use the headline env: XVIEW=1 XMODE=C XGATE=1 XPTR=1 XSHIFT=4 XREF=muvod STAGE1=geoset_rep_xs F0SEED=1 CROP=10000 CROPGATE=v2 REFSNAP=1.
- The flag requires --ref-snap and --ref-cam muvod. It refuses mode E (two-pass) and more than one GPU.
- Rejected a priori, so no GT selection among variants:
  - replay of the offline snap list (needs two passes);
  - M2 pointer swap (pointer cosine 0.33 vs 0.998 between consecutive frames, out of distribution);
  - M3 cond-frame insertion (evicts the frame-0 GT cond frame after 4 snaps);
  - in-tracker pre-encode hook (decides before cross-object non-overlap, so not on the PNG basis).
item3.rule:
Online, single pass, frozen S2-R6 constants: TAU 0.8, DELTA 4, DILATE 31; SCSam3/ref_snap.decide unchanged.

When it runs: in the runMVSeg main loop, right after the c_ini session yields frame t > start and its PNGs are written, and before session r+1 is advanced.

Which objects: every c_ini object that is NOT a crop target and has a non-empty mask_0. A crop target has 0 < prompt area < 10,000 px, known at frame 0. mask_0 = the frame-0 PNG = the GT prompt.

Decision: decide(mask_0, written mask_t, I_0, I_t), with I read from Video/<c_ini>/%06d.jpg exactly as snap_in_place reads it.

On a snap:
- Encode mask_0 on frame t's cached features the way the frame-0 prompt is encoded: video res -> 288 antialias -> 1008 -> >0, is_mask_from_pts=True, i.e. binary x20-10.
- Keep the entry's object_score_logits, obj_ptr, iou/eff_iou scores and maskmem_pos_enc.
- copy_ the result IN PLACE into non_cond_frame_outputs[t]['maskmem_features'] of c_ini's tracker state. The per-object slices share storage, so it must be in place.

The PNG rule is untouched: snap_in_place still runs after the crop pass. As a result the injected set equals the final snapped set minus crop-target objects exactly, feedback included (checked by Z2).

Why crop targets are excluded:
- Their PNGs, and the small-object PNGs of their neighbours, come from crop sessions that never read this memory.
- Their registered snap decision uses the crop mask, which does not exist online.
- They hold 1,399 of the 4,580 headline snaps.

Adoption: M vs H under the E8 section-5 rule, read unrounded, all 17 scenes scored, all watch values passing:
- basic delta > 0 and the 95% scene-bootstrap CI lower bound > 0 (E7.paired, 10k resamples, seed 0);

UNDERPOWERED from the step-0 gate is a result, not a failure.

designs.rationale:
Mechanism first. The facts below were checked in this session.

Item 3 (memory injection):
- Encoding mask_0 into memory can be done online and exactly. The probe re-encoded stored masks bit for bit, and the injection point is right after c_ini yields, before r+1 reads.
- The intervention is small: memory changes by about 2%. I recomputed PNG XOR/union on Blocks M1: 0.45% on c_ini unsnapped frames, 0.06% on cam0, 0.10% on cam9.
- Only 2 of the 34 scored non-reference views are direct neighbours of c_ini.
- So the expected effect is +0.01 to +0.04 basic. The registration is built to answer why, not just whether:
  - the online rule is an exact subset of the final PNG snaps (3,181 of 4,580 in the headline; crop targets excluded);
  - arm S cuts the direct cross-view read, so self vs cross-view vs feedback can be separated;
  - c_ini is split into frame classes, and other cameras by chain distance;
  - the cone gives a GT-free check.
- Only M is a candidate (E8 rule), so nothing is chosen on the GT.

Item 4 (generalisation):
- The MUVOD paper confirms that static objects were annotated in the first keyframe and propagated. 3 annotated cameras per scene, so G1 has 34 views.
- From the design data I computed: per-snap gain +2.53 on GT-identical frames vs +2.22 on non-identical frames, scene-cluster g_ref +2.00 (SD 1.30), gate precision 91.7%. These fix the NULL bound and the power assumptions in advance.
- G1 is free and tests camera transfer. G2 (MOVi-D: static camera by construction, per-frame metadata, rendered truth, 1.75 GB for 16 shards) tests gate precision and the redraw loss with no annotation process. G3 (MOSE static subset) tests real, independently annotated video.
- Populations, the static definition and a GT-free power gate are fixed before any scoring, so a null is informative. DAVIS is dropped because its gate passes 0/205, so a null there is guaranteed.

One arm only: S2-R7 'Rm', which replays the registered snaps into the tracker memory using encoding M1.
- Folder: SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgeoset_rep_xsFsCs10kG2RsRm.
- Command, per scene: XVIEW=1 XMODE=C XGATE=1 XPTR=1 XSHIFT=4 XREF=muvod STAGE1=geoset_rep_xs F0SEED=1 CROP=10000 CROPGATE=v2 REFSNAP=1 REFSNAPMEM=1 ./runMVOptThree.sh <scene>.

Variants declared now as NOT run, so none can be picked after the results are known:
- M2 (also replace obj_ptr): the pointer jumps to cosine ~0.33 against 0.998 between consecutive frames, which is out of distribution.
- M3 (make snapped frames conditioning frames via add_new_mask): this changes the cond-frame regime. Up to 21 cond frames per object; the frame-0 GT cond frame leaves the 4-frame cond attention after 4 snaps; and it reads like interactive correction.
- B (online decision on the mainline mask): its decision basis differs from the registered rule for the 1,249 of 4,580 snaps on crop-kept c_ini objects, and memory feedback flips borderline-tau decisions.

item3.rule:
Injected set
- I(scene) = provenance.ref_snap.snapped_files from the base folder's MANIFEST. Verified: 4,580 entries over 17 scenes.
- These are the registered S2-R6 decisions (TAU 0.8, DELTA 4, DILATE 31), taken on the headline's final PNGs, crop-kept objects included. No new decision is made anywhere.

Injection
- When: in the lockstep loop, right after the c_ini session yields frame t > start and its PNGs are written, and before any other session advances.
- For each (t, obj) in I, take mask_0 = obj's frame-0 PNG on c_ini (= the GT prompt).
- Prepare it by the same route as the frame-0 conditioning mask: video resolution -> 288 bilinear with antialias -> 1008 bilinear -> >0. Use is_mask_from_pts=True, i.e. a binary mask scaled to +-10 by the configured x20 -10.
- Encode it with tracker._encode_new_memory on c_ini's still-cached frame-t features.
- copy_() the result in place into that object's non_cond_frame_outputs[t]['maskmem_features']. In place is required because per-object slices share the tensor.
- Keep maskmem_pos_enc, obj_ptr, object_score_logits and the iou/eff_iou scores. The entry stays non-conditioning; snapped entries have eff_iou >= 0.93, so memory selection and the G gate always admit them.

Everything else is unchanged
- The crop pass runs as now (it does not depend on mainline memory).
- --ref-snap then applies the Rs rule to the final PNGs. Its snap set may differ from I through feedback; this is reported, not forced.

Refusals
The run refuses when any of these holds:
- no --ref-snap
- ref-cam is not muvod
- --two-pass / mode E
- more than one GPU
- algo is not MVOpt
- the base MANIFEST is missing, or its method is not this method without 'Rm'
- the base content_digest differs from the value written into the registration

MANIFEST block ref_snap_mem: base path and digest, n_injected, the injected list, seconds.

Stop rule: one run. If it is not adopted, item 3 closes as 'no effect'. No other variant (M2, M3, B) is run on MUVOD without a new registration that declares itself a second look on the same test set and is judged with a 97.5 % CI.

Primary
- basic Δ with a 95 % scene-bootstrap CI (Random(0), 10,000)
- per-scene Δ and the worst scene
- complete Δ

Watch values: GT-free, computed before scoring; any failure means no verdict.
- Z1: injected count equals |I| exactly; each entry is injected once; nothing outside I is injected.
- Z2 (cone byte identity): let t* be the first injected frame and r the c_ini index in the run's own session order. Every PNG and view_areas entry outside the predicted cone must be byte-identical to the base. That is frame 0 in every view, c_ini frames <= t*, and view r-k frames < t*+k; views above r may change from t*. The cone was measured on Blocks and CoffeeMartini by the probe.
- Z3: crop-pass targets, verdicts, areas and the crop-kept PNGs are byte-identical to the base.

P1: basic Δ in [-0.03, +0.05]. Most likely verdict: not adopted (CI contains 0), P ≈ 0.75.
P2: c_ini contribution in [-0.01, +0.04]; non-reference contribution in [-0.02, +0.02].
P3: complete Δ within ±0.05.
P4: worst scene >= -0.2; no scene with |Δ| > 0.3.
P5: in >= 15 of 17 scenes, PNG XOR/union <= 1 % on c_ini non-snapped frames and <= 0.3 % on the other scored cameras; <= 20 PNGs with IoU < 0.5 against the base (the CoffeeMartini probe had 1).

Basis
- Injection changes the memory by a median 2.1 % of its norm, against ~33 % natural frame-to-frame change.
- Static-object loss per frame does not grow over time: 0.0272 at t=1, when memory holds only the GT prompt, vs 0.0248 at t=20. So putting mask_0 in memory cannot remove the redraw loss.
- The reachable unsnapped c_ini loss is 0.343 (hard ceiling); the realistic bound is +0.01 to +0.04.
- Only 2 of 34 non-reference views are direct neighbours of c_ini. Switching cross-view memory off and on moves those views by a mean of 0.0008 J&F.

- Code: about 0.5 day (module, flag, REFSNAPMEM in runMVOptThree.sh, tests in the style of tests/test_pipeline_inprocess.py).
- GPU: about 2.1 h in total:
  - smoke: Blocks ~3 min and CoffeeMartini ~15 min
  - sweep: 17 one-scene jobs, ~1 h 45 min, under gpu.lock. The longest jobs are FlameSteak (~15 min) and CoffeeMartini (~14 min), all under 25 min, from the E14 log mtimes.

item3.risks:
(1) Test-set reuse. This is another stage-2 decision on the same 17 scenes, with no stage-2 dev set. One a-priori arm, frozen constants and the stop rule limit it. A chance pass (a 17-scene bootstrap is mildly anti-conservative) would add a meaningless increment to a headline that was already tuned on the test GT; the disclosure keeps Rs and Rm separate.

(2) GT leakage. Not a protocol violation: only mask_0 (the given c_ini frame-0 prompt) and the video enter memory, and mask_0 already reaches the other cameras through stage-1 seeding and through c_ini's frame-0 cond memory (mode C _lookup fallback). But the snap set comes from thresholds chosen on the test GT, so Rm carries a test-GT-designed decision into every camera (on Blocks, all views change by frame 5). LOSO does not cover that spread, so it must be disclosed.

(3) Moving objects. Memory anchored on mask_0 could slow tracking once an object starts moving after a run of snaps (442 moving-class frames after a stop, loss 0.164). The injected frames are ones where δ <= 4 said the object had not moved, so harm should be small. It is reported by class and guarded only by the scene line of -1.0.

(4) Conditioning semantics. M1 keeps the entries non-conditioning, so it adds no 'prompt' frames. A binary ±10 mask in a non-cond slot is mildly out of distribution (non-cond memory is normally soft), and obj_ptr stays the tracker's own.

(5) Not online. The replay needs the pass-1 headline run, and the method costs two passes if adopted.

(6) Baseline drift. Comparing against a stored folder assumes determinism. The Z2 cone check catches drift outside the cone only.

(7) Detectability. The expected effect is below the CI width (the S2-R6 CI half-width is ~0.15). A null result is the likely outcome; the run's value is closing the item with a measurement instead of an inference.

- D = the mean over all 17 scenes (Frog counts with 0).
- CI = e7_judge.paired (Random(0), 10,000).
- Reference R = +1.094: the c_ini per-view Δ of the registered S2-R6 pair (3 x 0.3645).

4a watch values (no verdict on any failure)

- Z2: the changed PNGs are exactly the snap list; each equals its view's frame-0 PNG; the counts are exactly 6,800 (H) and 6,489 (C).

4a secondaries, declared in advance

- Mean ΔJ&F per snapped object-frame.
- D under the complete protocol.

- Static subset S, by the definition fixed on 2026-10-16 before any computation (scratch s2r6x/STATIC_DEF.txt): background = pixels outside a 31 px disk dilation of the frame-0 mask union; static if max over t in {10, 20} of median |I_t - I_0| <= 4 AND the phase-correlation shift <= 1 px.

item4.pass_rule:
4a: a check that the thresholds transfer within MUVOD. The reading is asymmetric and fixed in advance.

Verdict, from arm H only
- TRANSFERS: D_H > 0, CI lower bound > 0, D_H >= 0.5R = +0.547, and worst scene >= -0.51. (-0.51 is the refloss harm mark of -0.17 basic, put on the per-view scale.)
- WEAK: CI lower bound > 0, but not TRANSFERS.
- DOES NOT TRANSFER: CI lower bound <= 0.
- Arm C is reported but has no vote.

What each verdict allows
- TRANSFERS allows only: 'the frozen thresholds also help the other annotated views of the same scenes'. Never 'generalises'. It does not drop or shrink the LOSO +0.387 caveat and changes no headline.
- DOES NOT TRANSFER: every Rs report adds that line. The Rs adoption is not re-judged; that was a different test, already decided.

4b
Gates before scoring:
- F1 (GT-free, before tracking): |S| >= 30 videos AND prompt-only δ-gate passes >= 600 object-frames in S.
- F2 (GT-free, after tracking): Rs snaps >= 300 object-frames in S.
- If either fails: 'not testable', and the GT stays sealed.

Verdict on Δ_S:
- REPLICATES: CI lower bound > 0, Δ_S >= +0.1, and <= 5 % of S videos have Δ < -1.0.
- HARMFUL: CI upper bound < 0, or > 10 % of S videos have Δ < -1.0.
- Otherwise NO DETECTABLE EFFECT, reported with the minimum detectable effect (2 x the bootstrap SE).

Secondary: mean ΔJ&F per snap against MUVOD c_ini's +0.0245, and the external GT's share of masks identical to frame 0 (computed after scoring), to state which annotation style was tested.
