designs.rationale:
Approach: risk first. For each item I asked how it could mislead, and kept only the designs that survive those checks.

Item 3 can be made honest, so GO, but narrowly:
- It must be one variant chosen in advance, because no stage-2 dev set exists to choose among variants.
- The chosen variant is the snap replay. Its decisions are exactly the registered S2-R6 ones, so it introduces no new rule and measures the memory effect alone.
- Its encoding is the frame-0 conditioning route, and the entries stay non-conditioning. This avoids the problems of making snaps conditioning frames (M3: the frame-0 GT drops out of attention, and it reads like interactive correction) and of an online decision (it cannot reproduce the registered basis for the 27 % of snaps on crop-kept objects).
- It adds no information beyond the given frame-0 prompt and the video, so it is not a protocol violation. But it does spread a decision whose thresholds were chosen on the test GT into every camera, and the LOSO estimate does not cover that. It therefore needs its own disclosure line.
- Expected effect is tiny: +0.01 to +0.04 on c_ini and about 0.005 or less elsewhere. Memory changes by ~2 % of its norm; static loss per frame does not grow when memory holds only the prompt; and only 2 of the 34 non-reference views neighbour c_ini. So the registration predicts a null, and the stop rule bars trying the other variants afterwards.

Item 4 cannot meet its real goal (independent data) right now.
- 4a, the within-MUVOD pseudo-reference test, costs nothing and is registered with an asymmetric reading: a fail is informative; a pass only shows that the thresholds transfer across views of the same scenes. The reason is MUVOD's annotation: the MUVOD paper confirms static masks are propagated from the first keyframe, 48-49 % of object-frames are pixel-identical to frame 0 on every camera, and the δ decisions agree with c_ini's.
- 4b, MOSE static subset: designed with GT-free feasibility gates and sealed GT, but NO-GO until the user approves the 22 GB download and the licence.
- DAVIS: NO-GO, because the rule never fires on it.

What I verified myself:
- 3 annotated cameras per scene, not 4 as the task text said, so 34 non-reference views.
- 4,580 headline snaps in the manifests.
- The pseudo-reference snap counts.
- Camera distances to c_ini: 2 / 6 / 26 views at distance 1 / 2 / 3 or more.
- Lockstep write order: crop pass, then ref-snap.
- The crop gate does not depend on mainline output.
- Encoder input: binary when is_mask_from_pts, otherwise sigmoid.
- Per-scene times all under 25 min (FlameSteak about 15 min).
- The SegProject/Data folder on the NAS mirrors local Data/.
- The MUVOD annotation text.
- SAM 2's training data.

Discrepancies found:
- The task text claims 4 annotated cameras; there are 3.
- SCSam3/ref_snap.py cites tests/test_ref_snap.py, which does not exist; the pin is in tests/test_pipeline_inprocess.py:152.
- The DAVIS reads probably exceeded the 50 MB cap.

No tracked file was touched. My scratch files are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-sjpark-Documents-SCSegmentation/8f2081e6-71f6-4db0-ab8a-894e91d89bb3/scratchpad/s2r6x/reg/ (gt_ident.py, gt_ident_t.py, gt_ident.json).

assessments.item: item 3 (replay registered snap list into memory, M1)
assessments.verdict: Honest and implementable, but only my second choice. Registering it is acceptable if the user prefers a pure memory-effect measurement over a method that can be deployed.
assessments.problems: Checked and confirmed: 4,580 entries; the per-scene counts sum correctly; the list sha256 is 55a68c32...a4f6 (sorted '<folder>/<cam>/<t>/<obj>.png' joined by '\n', no trailing newline). The encoder binarises when is_mask_from_pts, then x20-10 (sam3_tracker_base.py:821-830). Only score>0 matters for no_obj_embed (:844-847), so stored score vs +10 is irrelevant. The probe M1 on Blocks equals the headline list, so the G2 byte-identity gate is feasible. The probe's observe run is byte-identical to the headline (951/951), and M1's cone and XOR values match (cam4 first change at f2 0.51 %, cam0 at f5 0.09 %, cam9 at f1 0.11 %). All 1,249 crop-kept replay entries have a non-empty mainline mask (view_areas), so Z1 'score>0' will hold. Problems: (1) If adopted, the headline becomes a two-pass pipeline (about 2x GPU) that needs a prior run of the same config. (2) The replayed crop-kept decisions depend on the crop gate v2 verdict, which counts window-edge frames over all 21 frames. Memory at t therefore uses information from later frames; this is not a protocol breach, but the method is not causal. (3) If it passes, the deployable one-pass version would need a second look at the same test set. (4) The Frog smoke takes about 2 min (log 06:08:35 to 06:10:35), not 5. Predictions (basic Δ in [-0.03,+0.04], XOR <= 1 %) and cost (17 jobs, longest FlameSteak 14.9 min, sweep 1 h 43 min) are plausible. The E8 rule is well defined.

assessments.item: item 4 (4a: frozen rule on 34 held-out annotated views; external data deferred)
assessments.verdict: Recommended basis for item 4a, with one implementation fix. Its handling of the external data (deferred to the user) is correct.
assessments.problems: Checked: 3 annotated cameras per scene, so 34 held-out views. My own GT-free recount with ref_snap.decide on SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgtFsCs10kG2 gives 6,800 / 13,205, per scene exactly as in its Z1 (Frog 0). All 662 held-out frame-0 PNGs equal GT==obj. snap_in_place takes any camera name, so calling it on non-c_ini cams works unchanged. e7_judge basic = objects -> cameras -> scene, so per-view Δ for 2 changed views = 1.5 x basic Δ, and the size reading against 1.094 = 3 x 0.3645 is on the same scale. Fix: a whole-folder hard-link copy also links the top-level MANIFEST.json. Writing it with open('w') would truncate the source folder's MANIFEST, so the script must link per camera (as MVSeed/s2r6_snap.py does) or unlink before writing. Weak independence (same scenes and annotation process; the MUVOD paper confirms that static objects are annotated on the first keyframe and propagated) is stated honestly. The pass rule reuses E8 constants (no new constant). Predictions (basic Δ +0.25..+0.80) agree with snaps per view (200 vs 270 on c_ini). Cost (about 15 min CPU, 0 GPU) is plausible.

assessments.item: item 3 (online M1 decisions, crop targets excluded; diagnostic shadow arm S)
assessments.verdict: The candidate arm M is the one I recommend registering. Drop arm S, and drop Z5 as a validity gate.
assessments.problems: Checked: 1,399 of 4,580 snaps fall on c_ini crop targets (1,249 on kept targets, 150 on reverted ones). That leaves 3,181 non-target snaps, which matches P1. CropSmall writes only the (cam, obj) PNGs of kept targets (runMVSeg.py:1131-1137). So for non-target objects the final PNG equals the mainline PNG written at frame t, and Z2 ('injected = final snapped_files minus crop-target objects, exactly') holds by construction, feedback included. Targets are fixed at frame 0 from the GT prompt area (crop_track.select_targets_from, 0 < area < max_px). The mode C reads are confirmed (xview_gather.py _frame_for: v-1 at t, v+1 at t-1). Problems: (1) Arm S costs another ~1 h 45 m of GPU to decompose an effect predicted to be null. It also does not isolate the self channel: in S, neighbours still read c_ini's later, non-injected entries, which already carry the injected memory. So S's c_ini contribution is not 'self only'; only M-S is a clean quantity (the direct read). (2) Z5 (median memory change in [0.5 %, 6 %]) turns a prediction into a validity gate. A real 7 % would block the verdict, so it belongs in the predictions. (3) No byte-identity implementation gate exists against the probe on Blocks, because the probe also injected Blocks' 20 crop-target snaps. Dog (0 c_ini crop targets) can serve instead. (4) An xview_gather edit would be allowed: MVOpt is the development package (runMVSeg.py:91-92).

assessments.item: item 4 (G1 held-out views + G2 MOVi-D + G3 MOSE, one protocol)
assessments.verdict: G1 is acceptable after a rename. G2 and G3 cannot be registered or run until the user approves downloads over 50 MB and the licences.
assessments.problems: The folder suffix 'Rp' collides with --repair-seeds (runMVSeg.py:298; existing Data/MVSeg/Blocks/SegMaskSam3XW1GPS4MRp). Both G1 source methods are confirmed in Data/MVSeg/jf_e7.json (51 rows each). MOVi-D facts confirmed from public GCS and dataset_info.json: 256x256 validation split is 250 videos in 64 shards, 6.98 GB total; 2 s at 12 fps; 10-20 static plus 1-3 tossed objects; camera position sampled and never moved. Licence unconfirmed. G2 is close to tautological for unmoved, unoccluded objects (the rendered truth is exactly static). It tests gate precision and SAM 3's redraw loss, not real-footage transfer, and the design says so. The classes HARM/TRANSFERS/NULL/RARE are well ordered but add new constants (0.25 x g_ref, 1e-3 metadata thresholds), which is acceptable a priori. Pre-registering the G2/G3 converter details before the data is seen will probably need errata. Three tiers in one registration is more than the item needs right now.

assessments.item: item 3 (replay registered snap list, M1; stop rule with 97.5 % CI for any second look)
assessments.verdict: Acceptable alternative, equivalent to the minimal design. Its stop rule and disclosure text are worth adopting whichever arm is registered.
assessments.problems: Same two-pass and non-causality caveats as minimal. The suffix 'RsRm' breaks the documented convention 'Folder suffix Rs, last' (runMVSeg.py:126, 364); use RmRs. It describes SCSam3/demoSCSam3*/ as frozen, but runMVSeg.py:91-92 says MVOpt is the development target and only the other packages are frozen; this does not affect its own design. Its cone check is correct. The smoke on Blocks plus CoffeeMartini (about 18 min, under 25) and the deletion of smoke outputs unscored are sound. FlameSteak 14.9 min and CoffeeMartini 14.1 min are confirmed from the E14 log mtimes.

assessments.item: item 4 (4a held-out views with asymmetric reading; 4b MOSE NO-GO until approval with F1/F2 GT-free gates)
assessments.verdict: Its structure is best for the external part (NO-GO now, sealed GT, F1/F2 power gates) and so is its asymmetric wording. Its 4a thresholds need fixing; I prefer minimal's E8-constant rule.
assessments.problems: (1) It uses the 'Rp' suffix, which collides with --repair-seeds. (2) The worst-scene line '-0.51 = -0.17 basic on the per-view scale' is wrong for a statistic that is the mean of 2 changed views. That conversion is x1.5 (-0.255); x3 applies only to a one-camera change. (3) D_H >= 0.5R adds a new constant; it is a priori and harmless, but not needed. (4) Its GT-identity share of 48.0 % (6,995 / 14,560) uses a different denominator from the 13,205 scored object-frames (the anatomy gives 44.4 %), so a registered split must fix the object set. (5) Its claim that PlenopticServer2/SegProject/Data mirrors local Data/ is confirmed by a single top-level ls. Its 4b MOSE stance (no DAVIS, no MOSEv2, F1 |S| >= 30 and F2 >= 300 snaps) is sound.

judges.recommendation:
ITEM 3: GO, with one registered candidate arm: mechanism's arm M, without arm S. The reason I prefer it over minimal/skeptic's replay is practical. Both are honest, and the predicted effects are almost the same. But the online version is one pass and can be adopted directly. A replay pass would mean a two-pass headline whose crop-kept decisions also use the full-window crop gate, and turning it into a deployable method would cost a second look at the same test GT. The replay's extra 1,399 entries reach the output only through non-overlap and neighbour reads, because crop PNGs overwrite those objects.

Register docs/stage2-R7-prereg.md and commit it before the sweep. GT-free smokes may run before the commit. Rule text:

"Arm O = SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgeoset_rep_xsFsCs10kG2RmRs = the headline command plus --ref-snap-mem (REFSNAPMEM=1). The flag requires --ref-snap, --ref-cam muvod and MVOpt; it refuses mode E/two-pass and more than one GPU. Suffix Rm goes before Rs (Rs stays last).

Injection: in the runMVSeg main loop, right after the c_ini session yields frame t > start and its PNGs are written, and before any other session is advanced. For every c_ini object o that is NOT a crop target (0 < GT-prompt area < --crop-small px, via crop_track.is_target at frame 0):
- decide with ref_snap.decide(m0, mask_t, I0, It) unchanged (TAU 0.8, DELTA 4, DILATE 31). m0 = the frame-0 PNG; mask_t = the PNG just written; I read as snap_in_place reads it.

Then non_cond_frame_outputs[t]['maskmem_features'].copy_(mf as bf16) in place.

Disclosure if adopted: 'Rs was designed on the test GT (LOSO +0.387, covers only the PNG snap). Rm feeds the same online decisions into c_ini's tracker memory, measured once under preregistration on the same 17 scenes with no stage-2 dev set: Δ x [CI]. item4.registration:
A) S2-R6H: the frozen S2-R6 rule on held-out annotated views of MUVOD. Commit as docs/stage2-R6H-prereg.md together with S2-R7, before any scoring.

1. Arms
- Source G = SegMaskSam3XW1CGPS4MSdgtFsCs10kG2.
- Rule arm G+'Rh' = G with SCSam3/ref_snap.snap_in_place(dst, Video/<cam>, cam, start_frame, np, cv2) applied unchanged (TAU 0.8, DELTA 4, DILATE 31) to each of the 2 annotated non-c_ini cameras.
- c_ini and unannotated cameras are untouched. Files are hard-linked per camera; MANIFEST.json is never linked and is written fresh.
- The same procedure on SegMaskSam3XW0MSdgtFs -> ...Rh is descriptive only, with no vote.
- The suffix Rh is unused. Rp would collide with --repair-seeds.

2. Statistic
- Score G and GRh in one eval/eval_jf.py call -> Data/MVSeg/jf_s2r6h.json.
- Δ per scene = basic(GRh) - basic(G), via e7_judge rows / scene_scores (objects -> cameras -> scene).
- c_ini contributes exactly 0, so per-view Δ = 1.5 x basic Δ.
- CI: e7_judge.paired, 10,000 resamples, Random(0).

3. Verdict (unrounded; all 17 scenes scored and Z1-Z4 passing)
- REPLICATES iff basic Δ > 0, the 95 % CI lower bound > 0, no scene Δ < -1.0, and complete Δ >= 0. These are the E8 constants; nothing new.
- HARMS iff the CI upper bound < 0.
- Otherwise DOES NOT REPLICATE.

Size reading (registered, descriptive): if the CI upper bound of the per-view Δ is < +1.094 (= 3 x 0.3645, the c_ini design value from the E8 pair), the result is 'smaller than on the design camera'; otherwise 'at design size'.

4. Watch values (GT-free, except Z3, which reads only the frame-0 GT, i.e. the prompt)
- Z1: per-scene snap counts equal the pre-count. Total 6,800: AlexaMeadeExhibit 1050, AlexaMeadeFacePaint 229, Barn 689, Blocks 229, Breakfast 145, CBABasketball 145, Carpark 272, CoffeeMartini 1352, Dog 181, Fencing 54, FlameSteak 1105, Frog 0, MATF 392, MartialArts 165, Painter 346, PoznanStreet 171, Welder 275. XW0: 6,489.
- Z2: the changed files are exactly the snapped list, each byte-equal to its frame-0 PNG. Every other PNG is a hard link to G; the file sets are equal; the source MANIFEST's sha256 is unchanged.
- Z3: all 662 held-out frame-0 PNGs equal GT==obj.
- Z4: c_ini rows and Frog Δ are exactly 0.

5. Consequences, fixed now
- (τ, δ, dilation), the headline and the LOSO line never change because of this test.
- REPLICATES adds exactly: 'applied unchanged to the 34 annotated non-reference views of the same 17 scenes (same annotation process; decisions agree with c_ini 92 %, kappa 0.84): +x [CI] per view'. It is never worded as 'generalises' or as independent data.
- DOES NOT REPLICATE or HARMS is stated next to every Rs report, and whether Rs stays in the headline goes back to the user.

6. Disclose
- Non-reference GT was read before:
  - D-refloss §5 applied this rule family to stage-1-seeded other cameras (-0.02 to -0.22), which set the c_ini-only scope (R6 prereg §1);
  - D-nonref §2-3 published the GT-seed held-out loss of 0.12-0.17 per frame.
- Computed during design: the GT-free counts, the decision agreement, and the GT-identity shares.
- The source folders are E7-era code (2026-09).
- A positive result is largely expected.

7. Predictions
- basic Δ in [+0.25, +0.80] (80 %), point estimate +0.50; per-view Δ about +0.75 against the design +1.094;
- P(REPLICATES) about 0.85;
- >= 13 of the 16 non-Frog scenes go up; worst scene >= -0.3;
- complete/basic in [0.7, 1.1];
- mean ΔJ&Fx100 per snapped object-frame in [+1.0, +2.6];
- the share of Δ on frames whose GT_t is pixel-identical to GT_0 (denominator: total Δ over snapped basic object-frames) in [50 %, 80 %].

8. Descriptive only
The XW0 arm, per-scene table, per-snap Δ, the GT-identical split, and copy-GT0 classes.

B) S2-R6X: independent data. A template, committed only after user approval, separately per source, before the data are converted or screened.
1. Fetch and seal
- Stream once and record the archive sha256 (MOSE: 027b1608…585).
- Keep frames 00000-00020 of the >= 21-frame videos.
- Move the GT of frames 1-20 to a sealed folder outside the run tree, with a sha256 list. It is not read until all runs and the feasibility record are committed.
2. Population S
The static-camera rule above (STATIC_DEF.txt), computed from the video and frame-0 GT only. S is published and committed before tracking. For MOVi-D, also the stratum 'unmoved by metadata' (position and quaternion change < 1e-3).
3. Runner
- The single-camera path, validated byte-identical on Fencing v4 (168/168 before the snap, 168/168 after, 33/160 snaps).
- Each video has a one-camera config with c_ini = 0, Video/cam0/%06d.jpg (original JPEG bytes), Mask/cam0/000000.png and MVSeed_gt/cam0/0/<id>.png.
- Command: runMVSeg.py --algo MVOpt --xview-window 0 --ref-cam muvod --seeds-from MVSeed_gt --frame0-seed --ref-snap --save-stages.
- Base = <out>_stages/stage2; arm = <out>. No crop pass and no cross-view; the 4a XW0 arm is the bridge.
4. Feasibility gate F (GT-free, from the run MANIFESTs, committed before unsealing)
Needs |S| >= 30 videos, >= 300 snapped object-frames, and >= 30 videos with at least one snap. Otherwise the result is UNDERPOWERED and the GT stays sealed.
5. Statistic
- eval/eval_jf.py (bound_th 0.008) on frames 0-20.
- Per-video J&Fx100 = mean over objects; D = mean over S of (arm - base); CI by a 10,000-resample video bootstrap, Random(0).
6. Verdict
- REPLICATES iff D > 0 and CI lower > 0;
- HARMS iff CI upper < 0;
- otherwise NO DETECTABLE EFFECT, reported with its CI (the minimum detectable effect).
7. Descriptive
- all >= 21-frame videos;
- per-snap g against the design value +2.45 per object-frame;
- gate precision = share of snaps with copy-GT0 J&F >= 0.98 (design value 91.7 %);
- short side >= 1080 vs < 1080, and size bins.
8. Consequences
- Never re-tuned; re-tuning would need a new registration that splits the data into dev and test.
- REPLICATES adds one line.
- NO DETECTABLE EFFECT or HARMS makes this line mandatory next to every Rs headline: 'does not transfer to <data>; the MUVOD gain depends on MUVOD's static-object annotation (first-keyframe masks propagated)'. Rs's place in the headline then goes back to the user.
9. Predictions for MOSE
|S| 150-450; snap rate in S 5-35 %; D in [-0.1, +0.5]; P(REPLICATES) about 0.35.
